statistics.locator: Results, ANOVA for the adaptation phase (between-factor Age, within-factor Episode)
statistics.quote: We confirmed these observations by analysis of variance (ANOVA) for the adaptation phase, using the between-factor Age and the within-factor Episode: significant effects were yielded for Age (F(1,22)=7.58, P<0.05), Episode (F(14,308)=41.14, P<0.001), and their interaction (F(14,308)=3.44, P<0.001).
statistics.direction_quote: Most importantly, adaptive improvement was more pronounced for young than for old subjects.
statistics.admissible_reason: Between-participant main effect of Age on pointing error across the 15 adaptation episodes (the perturbation block containing the late-adaptation endpoint).
statistics.notes: Main effect of Age over the whole adaptation phase (episodes 6-20), not a contrast restricted to the final adaptation episode; the paper reports no episode-20-only between-group test. Direction: old subjects had larger errors (exponential fits: y=9.92+53.51×exp(−x/5.89) young vs y=29.51+29.91×exp(−x/5.13) old).

statistics.locator: Results, ANOVA for the adaptation phase — Episode effect
statistics.quote: significant effects were yielded for Age (F(1,22)=7.58, P<0.05), Episode (F(14,308)=41.14, P<0.001), and their interaction (F(14,308)=3.44, P<0.001)
statistics.admissible_reason: Within-participant factor (Episode), not a between-group comparison.

statistics.locator: Results, ANOVA for the adaptation phase — Age × Episode interaction
statistics.quote: significant effects were yielded for Age (F(1,22)=7.58, P<0.05), Episode (F(14,308)=41.14, P<0.001), and their interaction (F(14,308)=3.44, P<0.001)
statistics.admissible_reason: Interaction term, not a simple between-group comparison.

statistics.locator: Results, additional ANOVA on pointing errors in episodes 20 and 26
statistics.quote: To determine whether the initial reduction of performance differed between age groups, we compared the pointing errors in episodes 20 and 26 by an additional ANOVA; the effects of Age (F(1,22)=13.78, P<0.01) and Episode (F(1,22)=7.79, P<0.05) were significant but not their interaction, in accordance with the view that the initial reduction was not age-dependent.
statistics.direction_quote: Most importantly, adaptive improvement was more pronounced for young than for old subjects.
statistics.admissible_reason: Age effect averaged over episode 20 (last adaptation episode) AND episode 26 (refresh phase), so it mixes the late-adaptation window with a later phase.
statistics.notes: This is the analysis that comes closest to the endpoint (episode 20 is the last adaptation episode), but it pools episode 20 with refresh-phase episode 26. Direction of the Age effect is not stated in this sentence; taken from the general statement about adaptive improvement.

statistics.locator: Results, ANOVA for the refresh phase
statistics.quote: Accordingly, ANOVA yielded significant effects of Age (F(1,22)=13.42, P<0.01) and Episode (F(2,44)=6.18, P<0.01), but no significant interaction.
statistics.admissible_reason: Different measurement window: refresh phase after the five-minute break, not the end of the initial perturbation block.
statistics.notes: Recorded for completeness; same measure (pointing error) but a different phase.

statistics.admissible_reason: No standardised effect size is printed for pointing error on these pages.
statistics.notes: These pages report only F and t statistics with P thresholds (no eta-squared, d, or confidence intervals). Exponential fit parameters (y=9.92+53.51×exp(−x/5.89) young; y=29.51+29.91×exp(−x/5.13) old) are curve fits, not standardised effect sizes.

parsed.notes: The paper reports no between-group test restricted to the final adaptation episode (episode 20); Fig. 1 shows means ± SD per episode but no numeric values are given in the text. Other statistics on page 3 concern different outcomes/phases and were not transcribed as this outcome: the after-effect ANOVA (Episode F(4,88)=66.84, P<0.001; interaction F(4,88)=3.95, P<0.01), the tracking-task transfer ANOVA (Procedure F(1,43)=144,09, P<0.001), and the trail-making test (t(22)=5.25; P<0.001).
